title: Why hobby programming communities resist LLM-generated work
friendlyTitle: Sometimes learning matters more than AI finishing the job
summary: Michael Fogus argues that many hobby programming communities value learning, mastery and explanation more than merely producing working code. In that setting, LLM-generated results can undermine the activity’s purpose, especially when users cannot explain or maintain what they submit.
friendlySummary: Some programming groups reject AI-made code because their main goal is to learn deeply and understand every part of the work.
whyItMatters: The essay offers a useful test for everyday AI use: decide whether the goal is the finished output or the skill gained by doing the work. AI can be a force multiplier for informed practitioners, but outsourcing the whole process may erase the learning or trust that matters most.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Before using AI, ask whether you want the result or the practice. If learning is the goal, use AI as a helper instead of letting it do everything.
